posts.title: Two Poems by Trevor Conway
posts.description: Fossil . These barcode strata, exposed by quiet collapses to daylight in a freakish era. Its caked waiting for some astonished recognition has been so patient, and then, imagine: . we surmise its most unassuming days from bone, a loose phrenology of crushed physique, where tooth and shadow corroborate an alphabet. . Its immortality was accidental – the crash of flood, tar or mud, a breathless shock of volcanic ash. . Brutal, yes. An ugly assault on all its senses, with no time even to mourn a what-might-be. No, nothing. . Of course, it never sought a fame so pedantic, could only envisage what lay ahead – certainly not these filthy layers shelving its crumpled afterlife to archive what little we know and pretend that time solidifies. . A Taste for Meat . As if they know, bending leaves into their mouths, that bodies yearn for protein, the chimps share a conspiracy of glances. . They rise together and creep along the forest floor. Colobus monkeys are leaping, chasing, above in their play

posts.title: Twisted by Phyllis Carito
posts.description: Twisted In one moment, our lives get twisted into a tornado, we don't know where it will drop us. As we get older these twisters seem more frequent and less random. We know they are after us. It is just a matter of time, we’ll slip away, singing “I saw some crazy things... instead of one head...*” I see my mother sitting by the window, rosary in hand as she is looking out but only seeing in, Head shaking No! Don’t remember. Still, she never forgets. Life is full of living and loss, and one inescapable death. And they don’t come back to tell us what is next Looking back is the absence in the presence, and we fight ourselves to aim to the future, but the yet-to-come has less to offer in our aging. Cycles, spirals, and seasons – how many are left? Before we are swept up and dropped in the unknown. *Joni Mitchell ‘Twisted’ Phyllis Carito: Published Spring 2026 by FLP: Rollercoaster of Life (full collection of poems) and accepted by Passager Journal a poem for their next poetry edition in S
